children: Palm oil rises in early Asian trading, driven by output worries amid El Nino conditions affecting both Malaysia and Indonesia, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. Technical analysis suggests CPO futures may see some consolidation or profit-taking near resistance levels, it says. The market is likely to adopt a buy-on-dips strategy as long as prices remain above 4,850 ringgit-4,900 ringgit a ton, it adds. AmInvestment Bank expects palm oil prices to face resistance at 4,956 ringgit a ton and find support at 4,891 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for November delivery is up 22 ringgit at 4,951 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
